advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Give the openai builder's httpx client a bounded connect timeout (e.g. `httpx.Timeout(read=float(cfg.timeout_s), connect=10.0, write=30.0, pool=10.0)`) so an unreachable endpoint fails fast, matching `_build_anthropic`.
evidence: src/rebar/llm/providers.py:264: `transport=httpx.AsyncHTTPTransport(), timeout=httpx.Timeout(float(cfg.timeout_s))`
src/rebar/llm/providers.py:209: `http_timeout = httpx.Timeout(read=float(cfg.timeout_s), connect=10.0, write=30.0, pool=10.0)` — the anthropic builder bounds connect separately
`timeout_s: int = DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_S` (config.py:506) defaults to 600, so an unreachable local endpoint could hang ~600s on connect
advisory.finding: `_build_openai` builds its httpx client with `httpx.Timeout(float(cfg.timeout_s))`, which applies the timeout (default 600s) to ALL phases including CONNECT, whereas `_build_anthropic` pins `connect=10.0`. Against an unreachable/misconfigured local server the connect attempt can hang for the full read-timeout window instead of failing fast.
scenarios: Operator sets REBAR_LLM_BASE_URL to a local server that is not running; the review call blocks on connect for the full timeout instead of failing quickly.
advisory.suggested_fix: Replace `httpx.Timeout(float(cfg.timeout_s))` with `httpx.Timeout(read=float(cfg.timeout_s), connect=10.0, write=30.0, pool=10.0)` to mirror `_build_anthropic`.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Either add transport-level retry to `_build_openai` (mirroring the anthropic tenacity transport) or document in its docstring that retry is intentionally omitted for opaque endpoints.
evidence: src/rebar/llm/providers.py:263: `http_client = httpx.AsyncClient(transport=httpx.AsyncHTTPTransport(), ...)` — no retry transport
src/rebar/llm/anthropic_model.py:111: `transport = AsyncTenacityTransport(` — anthropic path retries transient failures
The `_build_openai` docstring documents the timeout parity with anthropic but does not note the absence of transport-level retry
advisory.finding: `_build_openai` wraps a bare `httpx.AsyncHTTPTransport()` with no retry, while `_build_anthropic` wraps its transport in `AsyncTenacityTransport` (retrying 429/5xx/timeout/network blips below the agent loop). A transient hiccup from a local/proxy endpoint is not retried, unlike the anthropic path — an undocumented reliability asymmetry between the two builders.
scenarios: A LiteLLM proxy or vLLM server returns a transient 503; the anthropic path would retry, the openai path surfaces it immediately.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test asserting the openai builder's http_client is closed on session exit (and on a run that raises), mirroring test_session_closes_the_client_when_the_run_raises for the anthropic seam.
evidence: src/rebar/llm/providers.py:266 (and preceding): `self._closeables.append(http_client)` then `return _RebarOpenAICompatibleProvider(...)` — the openai builder owns a client the session must close.

tests/unit/test_llm_provider_factory.py:243 anthropic parallel: `assert built[0].is_closed is True, "the seam-built client leaked when the run raised"` and :208 `assert all(c.is_closed for c in opened)` — the discipline the openai builder lacks a test for.

search_files for `is_closed` and `aclose` in tests/unit/test_openai_compatible_provider.py returned no matches; test_bare_openai_string_without_base_url_builds_no_provider only asserts `_closeables == []` for the no-base_url case (providers.py never builds a client there), so the success-path closure of a REAL openai client is untested.
ABSENCE: no test drives ProviderSession(cfg-with-base_url) through a run and then asserts the built http_client.is_closed, nor asserts closure on a run that raises.
advisory.finding: The openai builder registers its httpx.AsyncClient as a session closeable (self._closeables.append(http_client)) but no test asserts that client is closed after a run, nor that it doesn't leak when the run raises — unlike the anthropic builder, which has both a success-path is_closed assertion and a leak-on-error test. Removing the append (or a close regression) would leak the connection pool with no failing test.
scenarios: A refactor drops or reorders `self._closeables.append(http_client)` for the openai builder — connection pool leaks per run; the suite stays green.
close() is changed to close only on the success path — an openai run that raises leaks its client, unnoticed.
